PLTR dropped ~5% after TCV growth collapsed from 138% in Q4 2025 to just 6%, dragging QQQ and XLK lower.

Investors splitting retirement accounts between QQQ and XLK may hold ~1.33% in Palantir, amplified by its 252x earnings valuation.

Building a portfolio and living off one are two completely different skills, and almost nobody teaches the second. This problem is what The Definitive Guide to Retirement Income helps, and it is free today. Read more here. (Sponsor)

Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR) dropped 4.89% in Tuesday's regular trading, recently changing hands at $169.62 by 10:31 AM ET. The drop followed a third-quarter earnings report that beat estimates on revenue and profit but showed bookings growth slowing sharply. Analysts pointed to a slowdown in total contract value. Part of this selloff hit the accounts of investors holding a Nasdaq-100 or technology sector fund.

Artistdesign.13 / Shutterstock.com
Revenue Beat, Bookings Slowed

Revenue came in at $2.313 billion against a $2.181 billion estimate, up 95.87% year over year. Adjusted EPS of $0.44 exceeded the $0.4072 consensus. Management also raised full-year revenue guidance to $8.530 billion to $8.534 billion.

Bookings measure the value of new contracts a company signs during a quarter. Revenue shows the work already delivered. Bookings show what customers have agreed to pay for down the road, so investors use them to gauge future revenue. Palantir reports this figure as total contract value (TCV).

TCV came in at $2.918 billion, up just 6% year over year. U.S. commercial TCV grew 11% to $1.463 billion, compared with 153% growth in the second quarter. Total TCV growth has slowed from +138% in Q4 2025 to +61%, then +49%, and now +6%.

Management blamed shorter contract terms. Dave Glazer, the company's finance chief, said, "We signed multiple eight-figure deals in the quarter that were shorter in duration than usual as customers rapidly adopted initial Sovereign AI capabilities in their enterprise." Total remaining deal value reached $13.4 billion, up 55%, and net dollar retention was 165%.

Shopify (NASDAQ:SHOP) shares are down 9.51% in today's regular session, trading at $141.37 as of 10:31 AM ET. The company reported third-quarter results before the open, and the sell-off has spread to several ETFs. If you own a Nasdaq-100 fund, you own a piece of this drop. If you own a plain S&P 500 or total-market fund, you probably don't. The difference comes down to where Shopify is incorporated.

alvarez / Getty Images
Revenue Narrowly Missed and Merchandise Growth Slowed

Third-quarter revenue came in at $3.742 billion, just below the $3.744 billion consensus, even though sales grew 31.58% year over year. Adjusted EPS of $0.49 beat the $0.4598 estimate. Gross profit grew 28.04%, slower than revenue, because the mix continues changing toward lower-margin payments revenue.

Wall Street's biggest worry is slowing merchandise sales, a point Barron's noted this morning. Gross merchandise volume (GMV), the total value of goods sold on the platform, rose 29%. That compares with 32% growth in the second quarter. With the stock trading at a P/E of about 155, even a small slowdown matters.

Carson Group's Ryan Detrick warns that a decisive sweep by either party could unsettle stocks.

JPMorgan sees a roughly 0.5% S&P 500 decline if Democrats sweep Congress.

JPMorgan noted that the S&P 500 has historically averaged a 6.6% gain in the fourth quarter of midterm years.

Major US indices opened mixed on Tuesday as polls opened, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average falling 182.38 points, the S&P 500 gaining 0.11%, and the Nasdaq Composite rising 0.38% in opening trade.

According to UBS Global Wealth Management's CIO, midterms are not to be viewed as a binary market event. While the results could influence the medium-term outlook, UBS expects AI investment, economic growth, corporate earnings, inflation and interest rates to remain the primary drivers of stocks.

On Stocktwits, retail investors' sentiment was 'bearish' for the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) and the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ), while sentiment toward the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) was 'neutral.'

How Stocks Could React To Midterm Outcomes

According to Carson Group chief market strategist Ryan Detrick, markets could find relief once election uncertainty fades. "There's some anxiousness before these elections," he told CNBC, adding, "Once you are through it, it's a big relief, and markets tend to do pretty well."

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

However, the analyst cautioned that a decisive sweep by either party could unsettle stocks, as greater political control could lead to increased spending and concentrated power.

JPMorgan expects a Democratic sweep of Congress to push the S&P 500 down about 0.5% on Wednesday. Conversely, Wells Fargo Investment Institute's head of global equities and real assets, Sameer Samana, told CNBC that Republicans retaining control of both chambers could trigger a rally.

"From a certainty standpoint, the market knows what to do with Republicans holding both chambers," Samana said.

JPMorgan: Economic Factors Trump Midterm Results

JPMorgan Asset Management's research found that the S&P 500 returned an average of 9.2% in midterm election years since 1937, compared with 13.3% in non-midterm years, with higher realized volatility.

The firm noted that average returns were slightly negative in each of the first three quarters of midterm years before rising an average of 6.6% in the fourth quarter. Historically, markets have also begun rallying just under a month before Election Day, regardless of the outcome.

Investors put $7.27 billion of net new money into the Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X ETF (NYSEARCA:SOXL) in October, about 29.91% of its $24.31 billion in assets. The fund ended up falling 47.89% over the month.

Mario Tama / Getty Images

The ProShares UltraPro QQQ (NASDAQ:TQQQ) drew $3.49 billion, about 9.49% of its $36.79 billion, while falling 20.53%.

The downturn continued on November 2, 2026, when SOXL fell 11.52% to $68.17, and TQQQ dropped 4.11% to $59.46. After hours, SOXL quoted $69.70 and TQQQ $59.83, too small a gain to offset the day's losses.

Money arriving while prices fall suggests dip buying, which means adding to a position on weakness in expectation of a rebound. In funds that reset their leverage every day, that approach gets more expensive the longer the recovery takes (we wrote a free guide on betting with just a small slice of a portfolio, with the sizing and exit rules that keep it from hurting, here).

What October's Flows Actually Show

Net flows record money entering a fund but not who bought, at what price, or whether they still hold, so the total loss is unknown. Hana Securities counted $7.15 billion into SOXL in the week of October 12 to 16, second among U.S.-listed equity ETFs, as its price fell about 33%, and $810 million into TQQQ during a drop of about 16%.
